The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the grievous injuries sustained by him, in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 02.07.2023, at about 5.30 p.m, the petitioner was proceeding in a tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4520 SCCH - 26 3 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 as a cleaner, he was sitting next to driver seat and driven from Rajaramanna circle towards Hinakal,
in a rash and negligent manner, when reached near Basavanahalli Junction, ring road, Vijayanagara 4th stage, Mysuru City, due to his negligence of driving, lost control and dashed against the street light pole and turtle, due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Supriya Hospital, Mysore for treatment, wherein he has taken treatment from 02.07.2023 to 05.07.2023 and he has undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance charges, towards nourishment.
3. Further stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Cleaner and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, till today cannot attend his work and sustained permanent disability.

4. Further stated that, the accident was occurred due SCCH - 26 4 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 to rash and negligent riding of the driver of tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4520 and in this regard, the V.V.Puram Police have registered the case against the rider of said bike in Cr.No.142/2023 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
The 1 st respondent was the R.C owner of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4520 and it was insured with the 2nd respondent.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: After service of notice, Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Tribunal and he has been placed ex- parte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

6. The respondent No.2 Insurance company has filed objection contending that, it has issued goods carrying vehicle package policy to the Tipper lorry bearing reg.No.KA- 51-D-4520 and the liability is subject to terms and regarding the limits of liability, limitations as to use and SCCH - 26 5 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 person who was driving the said vehicle at the time of accident has valid driving licence, FC, RC and also subject to the provisions of MV Act.

The petitioner was traveling as a gratuitous passenger at the time of accident in the offending lorry and lodged a complaint on 3-7-2023 to VV Puram traffic police station, Mysore, but in order to make wrongful gain from this respondent, he is falsely claiming that he was traveling as a cleaner in the offending Tipper lorry at the time of accident.

entities.text: VV Puram traffic police station, Mysore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There is a violation of Section 158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act.
The insured has violated the statutory provisions and also express convenient of the policy conditions of the insurance and as such this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
For all these, this respondent has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
 SCCH - 26 6 M.V.C.No.7934/2023  ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 02-07-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., he was proceeding in a Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D-4520 as a cleaner, the driver of the lorry driven from Rajaramanna circle towards Hinakal in a rash and negligent manner and proceeding and reached nar Basavanahalli junction, ring road, Vijayanagara 4th stage, Mysore city, due to his negligence driving,
lost the control and dashed to the street light pole and turtle, due to this accident, he sustained grievous injuries all over the body as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
8. In order to prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 12.

PW-1 examined Dr.Ramesh.B -Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria hospital,
Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked 1 document as per Ex.P.13.
One Vishwas-driver got examined as PW-3.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 is examined its Administrative officer as RW-1 and got SCCH - 26 7 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 marked two documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2 and closed his side evidence.
9. Heard the arguments on petitioner side.
Perused the entire materials in available on records.

My findings to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1: At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely SCCH - 26 8 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
"Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
12.
In order to prove the actionable negligence, petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.

He has filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and has reiterated the averments made in the petition and has produced FIR, complaint, sketch, spot panchanama, MVA report, wound certificate, final report, discharge summary as Ex.P.1 to 8, SCCH - 26 9 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 by these oral and documentary evidence Petitioner proved that, there was an accident in which he sustained injuries.

13. On perusal of complaint along with FIR, it reveals that petitioner has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the complaint, V.V.Puram traffic Police have registered FIR against the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D- 4520.
14.

With regard to negligence, Respondent No.2 has mainly contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of the Tipper lorry, who had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Except the said contentions, respondent No.2 has not produced any materials to show the non-involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and negligence of the driver of the lorry.
15. Moreover, neither the owner nor the insurer of the offending Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D-4520 has challenged the charge sheet.
The I.O has filed charge sheet SCCH - 26 10 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 after completion of investigation based on the evidences available at the spot.

sentences.text: All the records indicate the negligence of driver of the offending Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D-4520.
Respondent No.2 has also failed to prove the allegations of the petitioner with regard to the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

From the above materials and evidences it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D-4520.

Hence,
Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar Card as per Ex.P.9 to consider his age at the time of accident.
In Ex.P.11, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 1-1-1995, the accident was occurred on 2-7- 2023, hence the age of petitioner is considered as 28 years at the time of accident.

Therefore by considering the SCCH - 26 11 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 evidence on record and opinion of the doctor, I am of the opinion that, the disability of the petitioner has to be taking into consideration for his physical disability to award compensation.
So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
18. In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was Cleaner in Tipper lorry and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent No.2 has denied the profession and income of petitioner.
The petitioner has not produced his Bank Statement or any documents to show that, he was working as Cleaner in Tipper lorry and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.

Hence it appears that,
except the oral version of PW1, nothing is available on record to consider the avocation and income of the petitioner as stated by him.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.

entities.text: Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service SCCH - 26 12 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore, in view of the above decision and the accident was occurred during the year 2023, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

19. PW.1 has stated that, due to accident he has sustained grievous injury i.e., fracture of left patella,
severe injuries to hand, head and other grievous injuries and underwent surgery i.e., open reduction internal fixation+TBW done under SAB on 3-7-2023, after necessary treatment discharged with an advice for follow-up treatment, restricted fracture movements, not to involve in any strenuous activities and for complete bed rest.
P.W.1 has deposed that, he has taken treatment at Supriya hospital, Mysore as inpatient from 2-7-2023 to 5-7-2023 for the period of 4 days.

P.W.1 has further deposed that, due to accidental injuries, he is suffering pain and agony, he cannot do his regular activities, he cannot discharge his duty as earlier to the accident and he has sustained disability, as such he lost his future earnings.

On the other hand, the advocate for the petitioner vehemently argued that the evidence of PW-2 speaks that the petitioner is suffering from permanent physical disability of 18% of left lower limb,
which is 9% to the whole body.
The petitioner became a disabled and unable to do his work as he was doing prior to the accident and sustained loss of future earnings.
In the absence of material documents it is difficult to prove that he was doing business prior to the accident.

sentences.text: As already discussed above, at the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 28 years.

Therefore, he comes under the age group of 26 to 30, the proper multiplier applicable to be the case on hand is '17'.
22.

As per Ex.P.6-wound certificate and Ex-P8 discharge summary, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that, in the said road traffic accident, the Petitioner had sustained transverse fracture of left patella and the said injury is described as grievous in nature.
The petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 2-7-2023 to 5-7-2023 for SCCH - 26 14 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 the period of 4 days at Supriya hospital, Mysore.
23. Dr.Ramesh B-
Orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as Pw.2 and through him outpatient record is got marked as Ex.P.13.
P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 23-1-2025 for disability assessment.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has complained of pain in left knee, difficulty to squat on floor, climb upstairs walk on slope kneel,
difficulty to do routine activities.
PW-2 stated that petitioner suffers from permanent physical disability of 18% of left lower limb which is 9% of whole body.
24. By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.2, it can be inferred that, he is not the treated doctor.
As such, this Tribunal is declined to consider the entire evidence of P.W.2.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in SCCH - 26 15 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability and the documents placed on record shows that petitioner is suffering from permanent physical disability of 18% of left lower limb which is 9% of whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
The petitioner is aged about 28 years and he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 6% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
25. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and in total he was inpatient for a period of 4 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain.
Hence, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.50,000/- would be just and proper compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
SCCH - 26 16 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 26. LOSS OF AMENITIES:-
Further on perusal of evidence of PW.1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained injuries and the same is mentioned above paras.
The petitioner was aged about 28 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 and also considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

sentences.text: ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.8, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Supriya Hospital from 2-7-2023 to 5-7-2023 for a period of 4 days.
The petitioner is aged about 28 years and he might have taken assistance from attender.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of Rs.6,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

28. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
SCCH - 26 17 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 As on the date of accident he was aged about 28 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs1,95,840/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 17 X 6/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.
29. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD AND REST PERIOD:-
With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, P.W.1 has deposed that, the doctors have advised him take bed rest and regular follow-up treatment.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that, he has taken follow-up treatment.

By considering 4 days as inpatient and follow up treatment taken by the petitioner on several occasions, around 02 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for two months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as Rs.16,000/- per month, SCCH - 26 18 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 Petitioner is awarded Rs.32,000/- towards loss of earning during laid up period.
30.
MEDICAL EXPENSES:-

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment,
Hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on Ex.P.11-medical bills for Rs.42,324/-.
The respondent No.3 has disputed the said bills.
On careful perusal of medical bills at Ex.P.11, it reveals that, the petitioner has paid amount towards medicines and treatment.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to medical expenses of Rs.42,324/- towards Medical Expenses.

31. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion is that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,56,164 /- under the following heads:
Sl. Compensation heads Compensation No. amount 1. Loss of future earning Rs. 1,95,840/-
capacity due to permanent disability

 32.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
33. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 insurance company vehemently argued that the respondent No.2 issued a Policy bearing No.610700312210009298 in respect of Tipper lorry.
The petitioner was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in Tipper lorry and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

In order to prove their contention, Administrative officer of respondent No.2 examined as RW.1. RW-1 deposed that, they have issued the policy in SCCH - 26 20 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-D-4520.
The insurance company has produced the policy as Ex.R2.
On perusal of the said documents, the policy was valid as on the date of accident in respect of Tipper lorry.
34. In this regard, the petitioner has examined the driver of the offending tipper lorry as Pw-3 and also Ex.P.7

Final report, it is clear that petitioner was proceeding in the offending lorry as a cleaner,
hence the defence taken by the respondent No.2 is not sustainable.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, Respondents being owner and insurer of offending vehicle, So, the respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to shall pay compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

opennyai_summary.facts:
: 
The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the grievous injuries sustained by him, in road traffic accident.
The 1 st respondent was the R.C owner of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4520 and it was insured with the 2nd respondent.
6. The respondent No.2 Insurance company has filed objection contending that, it has issued goods carrying vehicle package policy to the Tipper lorry bearing reg.No.KA- 51-D-4520 and the liability is subject to terms and regarding the limits of liability, limitations as to use and SCCH - 26 5 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 person who was driving the said vehicle at the time of accident has valid driving licence, FC, RC and also subject to the provisions of MV Act.
The petitioner was traveling as a gratuitous passenger at the time of accident in the offending lorry and lodged a complaint on 3-7-2023 to VV Puram traffic police station, Mysore, but in order to make wrongful gain from this respondent, he is falsely claiming that he was traveling as a cleaner in the offending Tipper lorry at the time of accident.
There is a violation of Section 158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act.
The insured has violated the statutory provisions and also express convenient of the policy conditions of the insurance and as such this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
My findings to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1: At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
"Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
12.
On the other hand, the advocate for the petitioner vehemently argued that the evidence of PW-2 speaks that the petitioner is suffering from permanent physical disability of 18% of left lower limb,
which is 9% to the whole body.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
With regard to negligence, Respondent No.2 has mainly contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of the Tipper lorry, who had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Except the said contentions, respondent No.2 has not produced any materials to show the non-involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and negligence of the driver of the lorry.
The petitioner has not produced his Bank Statement or any documents to show that, he was working as Cleaner in Tipper lorry and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.
In this case, the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service SCCH - 26 12 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 Authority, Bengaluru.
24. By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.2, it can be inferred that, he is not the treated doctor.
As such, this Tribunal is declined to consider the entire evidence of P.W.2.
It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in SCCH - 26 15 M.V.C.No.7934/2023 Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs1,95,840/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 17 X 6/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.
The petitioner was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in Tipper lorry and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
On perusal of the said documents, the policy was valid as on the date of accident in respect of Tipper lorry.
Final report, it is clear that petitioner was proceeding in the offending lorry as a cleaner,
hence the defence taken by the respondent No.2 is not sustainable.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, Respondents being owner and insurer of offending vehicle, So, the respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to shall pay compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
